title: Urgent stabilizer for kernel heuristic mis-selection causing token-rate collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-severity customer escalations reported across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private fleets: sudden drops in tokens/sec and 2-3x increases in TTFT for multi-tenant and single-tenant long-context workloads. Issue reproducible in canaries when heterogeneous context-window mixes were introduced to the kernel scheduler heuristic. This ticket tracks the immediate hotfix, verification, and short-term mitigations while we develop a durable scheduler calibration and telemetry improvements.
observed_metrics: p50 TTFT increased from ~180ms to ~420ms for affected tails; p99 TTFT spikes to 3.2s (baseline 0.9s); aggregate tokens/sec per-GPU dropped ~40% during bursts; request rejection/queue time rose on Dedicated pools by ~30%; affected models: quant-int8 variants of llama-* and smaller opt-style models under long context lengths.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported degradations (notably ACME Health and CartFlow). Hosted customers experienced transient slowdowns; Dedicated customers saw capacity pressure and increased queuing; Private installs with mixed model variants observed token throughput collapse under multi-context sessions. Business impact: degraded SLAs for two enterprise customers and 1 urgent escalation to Customer Success.
steps_taken: 1) Triage call with on-call infra, runtime, and SEs (2026-03-10 09:15). 2) Scoped reproduction in staging via synthetic mixed-context load (locust). 3) Identified correlation between scheduler's kernel-selection heuristic and heterogeneous sequence-length distribution. 4) Deployed conservative fallback (patch) to routing layer to bypass aggressive kernel heuristics and force conservative kernel for affected variants (canary region alpha). 5) Enabled temporary token-rate cap for non-enterprise tenants to protect Dedicated pools. 6) Customer comms sent for impacted customers with mitigation status and ETA.
root_cause: Scheduler heuristic was optimistically selecting high-throughput kernels based on stale aggregated stats that did not account for per-request context-length variance. Under mixed short/long sequence workloads and recent quant-int8 kernel changes, the selected kernels induced cache-thrashing and KV cache eviction storms leading to prolonged decoding stalls and throughput collapse.
short_term_mitigation: - Roll forward conservative selector (force-kernel: conservative) to all regions within 2h of canary validation. - Apply emergency KV-cache pinning tweak to avoid eviction storms. - Throttle per-session token admission for non-enterprise tenants by 20% to reduce pressure. - Increase autoscaler headroom for Dedicated pools temporarily.
hotfix_details: Patch rfr:github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/14209; changes: add 'selector_safe_mode' flag, update kernel scoring to penalize variance-sensitive workloads, add metrics emission for per-request context variance. Canary rollout: alpha->beta->global; initial canary = 5% traffic, observed metrics: tokens/sec recovered to 92% baseline, p99 TTFT reduced to 1.1s.
verification_plan: - Run 48h synthetic mixed-context soak with 1.5x baseline QPS. - Monitor: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 TTFT, KV cache eviction rate, scheduler re-selection count. - Customer smoke tests with ACME Health test harness. - Post-canary manual review and then progressive 25/50/100% rollout if stable.
rollback_plan: If p99 TTFT increases >10% vs canary baseline or tokens/sec remains <85% baseline after 30m of rollout, automatic rollback to previous selector with alert and page to runtime-oncall.
communication: - Notified CS/AMs and impacted customers 2026-03-10 13:00. - Internal status updates on #runtime-incident channel and weekly PM sync. - Drafted postmortem note for execs and customer-facing summary for ACME Health.
follow_ups: Add fine-grained per-tenant kernel telemetry (metrics + tags)
Long-term: redesign kernel scoring model to consider per-request variance and warmup history
E2E tests: add mixed-context stress tests in CI
Performance regression guardrail in PR pipelines for scheduler heuristics
notes: This incident highlights the need to treat kernel selection as stateful per-tenant workload rather than purely aggregate-optimized. We should avoid global optimistic heuristics without variance signals. Initial hotfix buys time; next milestone is metrics-driven selector replacement planned for Cycle 2026-W13.
